about.title: Foster City Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Foster City residents rely on nearby San Mateo County hospitals and clinics for everything from routine checkups to emergency care, and most visits go fine. But when a provider misses a clear warning sign, operates on the wrong site, or mismanages medication, the harm can follow a patient for years. California treats these cases differently than a car crash claim — a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in before a case can move forward, and there's a required 90-day notice to the provider before a lawsuit is even filed. We review medical records, walk you through what's required under MICRA, and explain what options may exist. There's no cost to get that conversation started, and no obligation to move forward afterward.

whyChoose.title: Why Foster City Patients Choose Us

items.title: We Know the Clock Is Different Here
items.desc: MICRA generally gives one year from when the harm is discovered, capped at three years from the original injury, and a 90-day notice must go out before any suit is filed. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so we move quickly to evaluate your case.

items.title: Expert Review Isn't Optional
items.desc: California almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, since a poor outcome alone doesn't prove negligence. We work with the kind of medical evaluation this standard demands.

items.title: Understanding the Damages Cap
items.desc: California law caps non-economic damages in these cases, though the cap rises each year under current law. We can walk you through how that cap may apply to your specific circumstances.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Foster City?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the harm, but never more than three years from the date of the original injury. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before a lawsuit can be filed, so the practical deadline is often earlier than people expect. We can help sort out where you stand.

items.question: Is a bad outcome from surgery or treatment automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result by itself doesn't establish negligence — there has to be a departure from the accepted standard of care that caused harm. This is why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to evaluate the records before a claim can proceed.

items.question: Does it matter which Foster City hospital or clinic was involved?
items.answer: The MICRA rules apply broadly across California regardless of the specific facility, whether care was received at a hospital along SR-92 or a clinic near Foster City Boulevard. What matters more is the timeline of your care and whether an expert review supports a departure from the standard of care. We can help evaluate the specifics of your case.
